results.title: Causal inference in drug discovery and development
results.content: ## Drug Discovery Today. # Keynote (green) Causal inference in drug discovery and development. Causal inference combines model and data to identify causations from correlations. We illustrate the iterative process of causal inference with a six-step model. Causal inference fuels both forward and reverse translation in drug discovery. To discover new drugs is to seek and to prove causality. As an emerging approach leveraging human knowledge and creativity, data, and machine intelligence, causal inference holds the promise of reducing cognitive bias and improving decision-making in drug discovery. Although it has been applied across the value chain, the concepts and practice of causal inference remain obscure to many practitioners. This article offers a nontechnical introduction to causal inference, reviews its recent applications, and discusses opportunities and challenges of adopting the causal language in drug discovery and development. His research focuses on developing methods for causal inference from multi-omics data. His research focuses on multiscale-scale causal modelling for risk-benefit assessment of drug candidates.

results.content: ## Moving from ‘what’ to ‘why’ to build robust, reliable, and truly intelligent systems. > tl;dr Current AI is great at finding correlations (“seeing”), but to become truly intelligent, it must understand cause and effect (“doing” and “imagining”). This post explains that causality is the key to building robust, generalizable, and trustworthy AI systems, moving beyond the limits of today’s correlation-based models. We’ve spent the last decade celebrating AI’s incredible ability to predict outcomes from data.
